(Let me preface this by clarifying that I love history and rare things FROM history. The meaning behind the items do not reflect my own personal philosophy)

Generations of my family were raised in the same small (less than 20k) country town.

I was in a flea market, sifting through whatever, and then I saw it. A silver amd green box, close to the size of a pack of cigarettes.

It was in a glass case, I found a worker with a key. Opening the glass, he motioned I take it. Slowly reaching in, taking firm hold and lifting the unexpectedly heavy box.

A silver finish on all sides but the top. Which had a small slate of green marble, maybe a quarter of an inch thick. Metal inlay and rope edge around it holding it firmly in place.

The bottom had been worn severely, right in the center. A brass color shown through the silver.

Opening it I'm surprised by the weight of the lid. It's 2/3rds the entire weight.

The owner saw what I had, left the counter and was obviously heading right at me. He told me his name, I recognized it through my grandparents, but I didn't know this dude.

He asked why I liked that piece. "Rarity, of course."

Long story short, it had belonged to his wife's grandfather. And had been told of why and how it was made after the daughters' father killed the Nazi guards.

The Jews were forced to make special goods for Ze Germans, this gorgeous cigarette case was such items.

However, it was supposed to be solid silver. As a "Fuck You" to the Nazi's, they made them only silver coated. Hence the discoloration on the bottom.

The silver wreath surrounding the golden swastika, that took up 1/3rd of the lid, was also diluted down.
That's pretty damn interesting, and pretty funny (the "fuck you" silver coat). Did you end up buying it? I'm surprised the person was selling it, honestly. Sounds like a family heirloom.
